title: What's new in BC-Bench
summary: This session covers what is new in BC-Bench, a benchmark that tests AI coding agents on real AL development tasks. It recaps the bug fixing category and shows that the AL MCP server improves agent results by almost 10% on pass@5, while the choice of agent harness matters little. It explains a contamination check that asks models to guess file paths without the codebase, and only 1 of 101 tasks matched. It then introduces a new code review category with three review approaches and an LLM-as-judge method, with results still being worked on. It closes with advice for partners to fork the open-source repository and run it on their own data.

chapters.title: Recap: what BC-Bench is and why AL needs its own benchmark
Bug fixing results and the AL MCP server
How partners can use BC-Bench and where to find it

features.name: BC-Bench evaluation framework
features.description: A reproducible evaluation framework for AI coding agents on real AL development tasks, used to measure the impact of changes to models, tools, instructions and agents. Its data sets come from real PRs and tests, are open source, and a research paper describes the details.
caveats: Only 400 open-source repositories are written in AL, compared with 3.3 million in Python, so general benchmarks like SWE-Bench do not reflect AL work

features.name: Bug fixing category
features.description: An agent is tasked with fixing a bug in the real codebase, using 101 tasks taken from bugs that human engineers fixed in the BC apps repositories.

features.name: AL MCP server for coding agents
features.description: The AL MCP server exposes AL tools such as compile, publish and search to coding agents, so they do not need VS Code open. With GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Opus, it improved pass@5 by almost 10% and the mean resolution rate, at the cost of longer runs.
caveats: Runs take a bit longer because the agent has to publish apps and run tests

features.name: Agent harness comparison
features.description: Using the same model, GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code showed no significant differences. The speakers conclude the choice of model matters more than the choice of harness on this data set.
caveats: Conclusion applies to the BC-Bench data set

features.name: Contamination detection
features.description: A check for whether models memorized the open-source BC apps solutions. The agent gets the repository name and bug description without the codebase and must name the files to modify. Across 101 tasks and three models with knowledge cutoffs after BC-Bench went public, only one task matched.
caveats: The one match was a task whose description contained the exact file path
Monitoring will be continuous, not a one-time effort

features.name: Code review category
features.description: A new BC-Bench category that tests whether AI can review AL code changes, motivated by fast-growing pull request volume on BC apps. Each task has an expected comment, and an LLM judges whether generated comments match it.
caveats: Results were still being worked on at recording time

features.name: Three AL code review approaches
features.description: BC-Bench compares a baseline with plain GitHub Copilot CLI, BC Quality installed as a plug-in on Copilot CLI, and the AL review agent. The AL review agent is a specialized orchestration focused on security, privacy and performance, and already comments on BC apps PRs.
prerequisites: GitHub Copilot CLI for the baseline and BC Quality plug-in approaches

features.name: LLM-as-judge review scoring
features.description: Unlike bug fixing, review comments are scored by an LLM acting as judge against the expected comment. In the example, two models flagged the unneeded log table line as concurrency and as performance, and both were judged correct.
caveats: Comments can look different yet still match the expected comment

features.name: Run BC-Bench on your own data set
features.description: Partners are advised to check the published results, fork the open-source repository, replace the data set with their own bug fixes, tests and PRs, and check for contamination if their repository is open source. The tool, data set and run results are open source on GitHub.
caveats: Published results come from the Microsoft data set, not the partner's own apps
prerequisites: Fork of the BC-Bench repository on GitHub
Own data set of bug fixes, generated tests and PRs
